chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad, from Ayoub ibn Harun, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'Did the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) part his hair?' He said, 'No. Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), when his hair grew long, it reached the lobe of his ear.'
ai.seo_question: What was the Prophet's hairstyle and did he part his hair?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) did not part his hair but allowed it to grow naturally until it reached the earlobe, establishing a specific aesthetic of modesty and dignity. This detail is significant in Shia fiqh for distinguishing between the Prophet's unique natural state and the general sunnah of grooming, influencing scholarly discussions on male hair length and styling in Islamic tradition.
